title: Multilingual Technical Support Voice Interface
business: Global technical support centers providing hardware troubleshooting for non-native speakers.
problem: Support agents struggle to interpret complex technical descriptions from users with thick accents or limited vocabulary, leading to high ticket resolution times and user frustration.
solution: Implementing the gpt-4o-audio-preview model allows the system to ingest raw audio input directly, bypassing the latency and potential data loss of intermediate speech-to-text transcription layers. By processing the user's voice directly, the model captures nuanced prosody and tone, enabling more accurate intent recognition and providing immediate, natural-sounding audio responses that guide the user through troubleshooting steps in their preferred language.
steps: Capture the user's audio stream via the client-side interface.
Format the audio data into a base64-encoded string for the Chat Completions API payload.
Send the request to the gpt-4o-audio-preview model specifying audio as both input and output modality.
Receive the response containing the generated audio content.
Stream the returned audio output back to the user's device for immediate playback.
outcome: Improved user experience through reduced communication friction and faster, more empathetic technical guidance without the need for manual transcription.
limitation: The model operates under a strict 16,384 max output token limit, which may truncate long-form technical instructions; developers should monitor the finish_reason in the API response to check if the output was cut off.

  messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "[base64_audio_data]"}],
  modalities=["audio"] # Requesting audio output
)
